intended_object: The category of coherent (left) modules over a ring R: the full subcategory of R-Mod whose objects are the finitely generated modules in which every finitely generated submodule is finitely presented. Inferred from the docstring, the name and the module documentation.
explanation: The definition is the full subcategory of `ModuleCat.{v} R` cut out by the object property `ModuleCat.isCoherent R`, which holds of `M` exactly when `Module.IsCoherent R M`. The library defines that class in `CoherentModules/Basic.lean` with the standard two conditions: `M` is finitely generated (`Module.Finite R M`), and every finitely generated submodule of `M` is finitely presented. `Module.FinitePresentation` is Mathlib's definition and is stated for semirings, so the definition makes sense for an arbitrary (possibly noncommutative) `Ring R`. This is the natural generality: coherent modules are defined for left modules over any ring, and the abelian-category structure needs additive groups, so a ring is the right hypothesis. The module universe `v` is left arbitrary, as in `ModuleCat`. The definition reuses Mathlib's generic `ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory` rather than rebuilding a category by hand. I found no notion of coherent modules or a category of coherent modules in this Mathlib version, so there is no counterpart to cite.
